newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA LEU FIRMS AS C.BANK STOPS DLR PURCHASES.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA LEU FIRMS AS C.BANK STOPS DLR PURCHASES.

text.p: Romania's leu closed firmer at about 7,200/260 to the dollar on Monday against 7,240/280 in early trading as the central bank (BNR) refrained from soaking up excess dollars from the market, traders said.
"The BNR did not buy dollars although the supply was high," said one trader.
Traders said the BNR had only taken leu funds from an overliquid money market at prices near 50 percent, higher than short-term prices of between 35 percent to 40 percent.
"I think the BNR drained less leu funds from the market than last week," said one dealer. Last Monday the BNR soaked up 525 billion lei in one-week deposits.
Some operators said the leu might continue to firm in the coming days if the BNR failed to mop up dollars as it had done over the past weeks in an attempt to stimulate exports.
"Foreign interest in Romanian equities is likely to pump in more hard currency flows," said a trader.
Other players said the leu might get under pressure from a drop in banks' deposit rates, which dipped due to slowing inflation and a cash-heavy money market.
"With interest rates falling, there may be some strain on the leu, with some operators taking fresh interest in the dollar as a means of savings," said one dealer.
The rates on individuals' one-month deposit fell towards an annual 60 percent from about 80 percent, after inflation had eased to 4.3 percent in May from April's 6.9 percent.
Licensed money changing bureaux quoted the leu weaker at 7,170/300 from about 7,150/300 in the morning.
